meanings.note: only when answering or making a phone call
medical institution for inpatient care

examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital.
He was admitted to the hospital.

examples.text: Все думают, ты в больнице. Откуда деньги?
examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital. Where did the money come from?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Used for women too. Common masculine noun meaning 'doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она там взятки для врачей хранит.
examples.trans: She keeps bribes for the doctors in there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Singular only. Common feminine noun meaning 'food, meal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.
Oh no, bad food? Does your stomach hurt?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Of a person: я занят = I'm busy. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').
of a place: здесь занято = it's occupied

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: + dative of the person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
A bell or phone. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Colloquial. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
Colloquial. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: поверить ему

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
Последний раз = for the last time. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, final').

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.
I'm asking for the last time. Where is the money?

meanings.note: Animate masculine noun in -тель. Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'traitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ничего я тебе не скажу, предатель!
examples.trans: I won't tell you anything, traitor!
The traitor revealed the secret to the enemy.

examples.text: Это ведь вопрос воспитания. Кого может воспитать предатель?
examples.trans: It is a question of upbringing, after all. Whom can a traitor raise?

meanings.note: Single act of betrayal. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to betray'.

examples.trans: I will not betray my native land.
I will not betray my native land!

examples.text: Твой дед в войну родину предал.
examples.trans: Your grandfather betrayed his country in the war.

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'steak' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пусть немного подождут свои горячие стейки.
examples.trans: Let them wait a bit for their hot steaks.

examples.text: Вот вкусный французский стейк и горячая рыба.
examples.trans: Here is a delicious French steak and hot fish.
Just like your steak from yesterday!

тереть.gloss: to rub, to scrub, to grate

meanings.note: Imperative три / трите. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rub, to scrub, to grate', paired with 'потереть'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rub, to scrub, to grate', paired with 'потереть'.

examples.trans: He tiredly rubbed his eyes with his hands.

examples.text: Аркашка, ты еле стираешь! Сильнее три!
examples.trans: Arkashka, you're barely washing! Rub harder!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
+ genitive singular: три дня. Core Russian num meaning 'three' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.note: in comparisons: больше, чем = more than

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
examples.trans: Why not? A sales assistant earns more than a lecturer.
